request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and `bin/e2e` passes.

**Front end:** the signed-in user is now sent to the server with each change, in an `X-User` header. I added a `user` argument to `postJson`/`putJson` in `api/http.ts` and to the four save functions (`addPerson`, `updatePerson`, `addClaim`, `updateClaim`). The person and claim forms take the name from `useCurrentUser()`.

**Server:** each of the four save routes has a new `audit` step that runs right after `save` and before `respond`, so it is covered by the same transaction:
- `people.POST.yml` → `AuditPersonAdded` writes `PERSON_ADDED … name=… grade=…`
- `people/{personId}.PUT.yml` → `AuditPersonEdited` writes `PERSON_EDITED …`
- `people/{personId}/claims.POST.yml` → `AuditClaimAdded` writes `CLAIM_ADDED … person=… amount=… date=…`
- `claims/{claimId}.PUT.yml` → `AuditClaimEdited` writes `CLAIM_EDITED …`

Two small helpers, `PersonAudit` and `ClaimAudit`, build the lines in the required order. The claim's amount and date are formatted by the same `ClaimResponse` code the screen uses, so the amount always shows two decimals and the date is yyyy-mm-dd. For edited claims the person's name is looked up from the store.

**Refused changes write nothing.** All checks (empty name, bad grade, name already in use, bad amount or date, missing person or claim) run before `save`. A refusal stops the request before it reaches the audit step, so no line is written. Any rule added later before `save` gets this for free. In the test, the refused `1.005` claim and the refused duplicate "Ada" left no lines.

Spring's `@RequestHeader` doesn't work in these OfficeFloor steps: it came through empty, and lines were written as `by=`. I used OfficeFloor's own `@HttpHeaderParameter("X-User")` instead, which works.
